minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard TC Passios renovation priced far above hopes and set FY22 budget hearing and warrant-letter schedule
minutes.summary: The committee discussed a member's request for salary, step and headcount data for town and school groups ahead of contract negotiations. It heard reports on the TC Passios building cost, capital planning and the fiscal policy review, and a finance director update on pension, health insurance and the governor's budget. It set the budget hearing schedule and the draft timeline for its warrant letter, approved prior minutes and adjourned.

public_comment.topic: A committee member's emailed request for salary, step, headcount and COLA cost data from town departments and the school side, plus comparisons with surrounding towns.
Closing public comment: none received by email and no hands raised.

votes.motion: Approve the meeting minutes of November 12th.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked for headcounts, salary schedules and the cost of 2 and 2.5 percent increases for each town and school group.
The preliminary renovation budget came in substantially higher than hoped, and the architects will look at ways to trim it.
The capital project dollar threshold is likely to rise, pushing smaller items into departmental budgets.
The pension assessment includes an unfunded liability portion that is paid off in 2036.
Monty Tech reduced the FY21 assessment, leaving money available to reappropriate or fall to the year-end balance.
The insurer's renewal range was announced and a full-month premium holiday is planned.
Unrestricted aid rises while Chapter 70 rises by less, and overall the increase is small.

decisions.decision: A member may email the superintendent and school business official to request school salary and headcount data.
A draft warrant letter is due on the 11th, with comments on the 18th and final review on the 25th.
Financial advisor and actuary will be scheduled for a 6 pm start on February 25th, the fire and police night.
The fiscal policy review is to be set aside for April.
The next meeting is February 11th, when the initial budget is presented.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard that the preliminary TC Passios renovation budget came in substantially higher than hoped, and the architects will look at ways to trim it.
A draft warrant letter is due on the 11th, with comments on the 18th and final review on the 25th.
A member may email the superintendent and school business official for school salary and headcount data ahead of contract talks.
The finance director reported on the pension assessment, a reduced Monty Tech assessment, health insurance renewal and the governor's proposed budget.
The fiscal policy review was set aside for April, and the next meeting was set for February 11th, when the initial budget is presented.

why_it_matters: A renovation price well above expectations for TC Passios could mean a larger borrowing or tax request for a building project if it is not trimmed.
A higher capital threshold would move smaller items into departmental budgets, and pension, health insurance and state aid figures shape the operating budget that taxes help fund.
